Une solidarité qui réchauffe à Rivière-d: Solidarity That Warms Hearts in Rivière-des-Prairies
En cette fin d’année, le centre communau: As the year draws to a close, the Rivière-des-Prairies community centre is delivering baskets to the homes of some 400 families in need.
Vendredi 20 décembre, j'ai eu la chance: On Friday, December 20, I was lucky enough to witness a large-scale operation carried out in just a few hours: the distribution of Christmas baskets to more than 400 homes in the city’s East End. This success is due in part to the impressive mobilization of volunteers. The sign read “Volunteers with cars wanted.”
Au départ, l'objectif de ce reportage ét: At first, the goal of this report was to meet the families and single people receiving the baskets. Their number keeps growing year after year because of the decline in purchasing power for a majority of citizens.
Le véritable défi consistait à entrer en: The real challenge was getting in touch with these mothers without making them feel ashamed of their precarious situation. On their doorsteps, these women above all wanted to express their gratitude to those who support them in concrete ways throughout the year. And they are right to want to do so when they speak to the media, because, as we know, the work of these community organizations, and its impact, can never be talked about too much. Enjoy the read!
<strong>En cette fin d’année, le centre: As the year draws to a close, the Rivière-des-Prairies community centre looks like Santa’s workshop. More than fifty volunteers are bustling about like true little elves to deliver generously filled baskets to the homes of some 400 families in need on Christmas Eve.
The atmosphere is especially festive. To the sound of lively music, some people grab a bite on the go while others get organized amid a cheerful hubbub filled with bursts of laughter. Baskets waiting to be distributed sit on long tables. One by one, drivers receive their route sheets while the boxes are carried to the trunks of their cars. It’s a true human chain. Everything is happening “with joy and good spirits, because you can feel that you’re doing something good,” sums up Nadine Félissier, development manager at Équipe RDP.
Pendant plusieurs heures, dans le statio: For several hours, cars and trucks stream through the parking lot, turning, for one evening, into Christmas sleighs.
« C’est vraiment incroyable de voir comm: “It’s really incredible to see how, in a neighbourhood like this one, people who sometimes don’t even have enough for themselves always find a way to give to others,” says one of the volunteers, who notes that word of mouth is working. “More and more of us are coming to help, and that’s wonderful.”
L’aide alimentaire n’est pas la mission: Food aid is not Équipe RDP’s primary mission. The organization is not affiliated with any food bank. It does, however, have the support of more than 80 partners, which it approached itself in collaboration with Les Racines d’Ena, a community organization it works with. They include Salvatoré, Roma, Saputo, the Fédération des producteurs d’œufs du Québec, Dame Sara, O’Sole Mio, Ikea and others. Several local businesses and many volunteers contribute anonymously to the collective effort.
C’est ainsi que depuis 2020, Équipe RDP: And so, since 2020, Équipe RDP has put together Christmas baskets every year: turkey, pasta, milk, soups, cereal, fresh fruit and vegetables, but also stuffed animals and toys. The recipients are families who, during the holidays, are not on the lists of food aid organizations.
La distribution de paniers est un prolon: The basket distribution is an extension of the work Équipe RDP carries out all year long. Its mission is to support children and teenagers whose families are in situations of severe hardship.
Dans le quartier, le travail d’Équipe RD: In the neighbourhood, Équipe RDP’s work is respected and considered essential by the community. As part of its support programs, psychosocial workers travel to schools every day to help struggling students. The aim is not to directly promote academic success, but to make sure their basic needs are met.
Les écoles du quartier jouent un rôle ce: The neighbourhood’s schools play a central role in identifying the most vulnerable families. When children show signs of distress or unease, school staff do not hesitate to refer them to Équipe RDP’s social intervention services. “Teachers and educators go through the principal to call on us. When a student behaves unusually at school, it’s often a sign that something is wrong at home,” explains Jessie Charles, a psychosocial worker with the organization.
Le fardeau de la précarité est particuli: The burden of precarity is particularly heavy for immigrant families seeking asylum, who most of the time live in run-down, overly small housing. Their apartments can be unsanitary and damp, furnished with furniture in poor condition, when there is any. In these cramped spaces, children play among toys scattered on the floor, between piles of clothes and cardboard boxes. “In these conditions, simply managing day-to-day life becomes a challenge. I look after about thirty families. The needs are enormous,” explains Jessie Charles.
Elle cite le cas d’un jeune particulière: She cites the case of a young person who was particularly restless in class. After speaking with his parents, she discovered that they forbade him from moving around the apartment where they live, for fear of disturbing the neighbours. Thanks to her intervention, mediation was set up with the neighbours.
« Parfois, les difficultés qu’un enfant: “Sometimes, the difficulties a child has at school are directly linked to tensions at home. School then becomes a strategic place to identify families’ needs,” adds Burt Pierre, another Équipe RDP worker. He stresses the importance of the role schools play in the early detection of problems.
Au-delà de la question matérielle, l’obj: Beyond material needs, the goal is also to restore balance in the lives of families in difficulty by giving them the tools they need to improve their daily lives, such as workshops on parenting in the context of immigration.
Les organismes comme Équipe RDPproposent: Organizations like Équipe RDP therefore offer much more than one-time assistance. They provide real help with the integration of newcomers and with the reintegration into Quebec society of local families who have dropped out of work, school or social services. The support ranges from French-language learning to financial management, including moral support.
Les intervenants travaillent main dans l: The workers collaborate closely with these families to help them find or regain stability. Their role is to build connections, reassure and offer concrete solutions to problems that can seem insurmountable. They also act as mediators between families and public authorities, making it easier to access services that are often difficult to obtain when you are an immigrant without status.
Les intervenants qui accompagnent ces fa: The workers who support these families in their daily lives often come from the local community and, through their closeness, bring an essential empathy. Many of them grew up in the neighbourhood and know the reality of the recipient families well, having lived it themselves in the past. This knowledge of the terrain allows them to forge strong bonds and create an atmosphere of trust, essential for help to be accepted without embarrassment.
Les paniers de Noël ne sont pas seulemen: The Christmas baskets are not just food aid; they are a symbol of the spirit of solidarity that animates this neighbourhood. Thanks to the efforts of Équipe RDP and the volunteers, these families in need will also be able to eat properly for a few days. Rivière-des-Prairies, faced with increasingly visible poverty, proves to be a powerful model that shows everything a united community can manage to accomplish. Despite growing economic hardship, notably rising rents, electricity costs and grocery bills, Rivière-des-Prairies continues to stand out for its strong solidarity.
Le moment de la réception du panier de N: The moment of receiving the Christmas basket is especially moving. The toys, cookies and little treats bring a bit of magic to the beneficiaries’ difficult daily lives. With a smile showing her gratitude, a mother of seven who arrived from Haiti about three years ago confides on the doorstep of her third-floor apartment in the building on Perras Boulevard: “We’re going to be able to celebrate Christmas and all have enough to eat!”
